background_notes.fact: For the supplied subring R⊂Q with fraction field Q and R-submodule J⊂C, the balanced multiplication map θ:Q⊗_R J→C is Q-linear, is injective, and has image span_Q(J). If c_1,...,c_m generate J over R, then 1⊗c_1,...,1⊗c_m span Q⊗_R J over Q.

background_notes.justification: Multiplication Q×J→C is R-balanced, so it induces θ. Every rational is a quotient of integers in R. For finitely many tensors write q_k=a_k/s_k with a_k,s_k∈R and s_k≠0, and let s be their denominator product. Tensor balancing writes their sum as (1/s)⊗c, with c=Σ_k a_k(∏_{l≠k}s_l)c_k∈J. If θ sends this to zero then c/s=0 in C, so c=0 and the tensor vanishes. Images of pure tensors are rational multiples of elements of J, and every such finite linear combination is an image. Expanding c in the finite R-generating family proves the spanning assertion.

background_notes.fact: A finite spanning family in a Q-vector space contains a basis, all finite bases have the same cardinality, and an independent family in Q^t has at most t members. For a free R-module L with basis of n elements and an R-algebra Q, those tensors 1⊗basis-vector form a Q-basis of Q⊗_R L.

background_notes.justification: Delete any vector lying in the span of the remaining vectors until the finite spanning list is independent. Finite Gaussian elimination shows that an independent family in Q^t has at most t members; applying this bound to coordinate isomorphisms in both directions proves invariance of finite basis cardinality, and also the strong rank condition for Q. For scalar extension, expansion in an R-basis gives spanning by its pure tensors. Each R-coordinate map extends to a Q-linear coordinate map on the tensor product, taking these tensors to the standard coordinate values; applying them to a zero linear combination proves independence. These facts justify the dimension and freeness steps at S002 without replacing M001.

background_notes.fact: For the supplied prime p and any nonzero rational q, there exist d∈Z and u∈Q with q=p^d u such that u and u^(-1) both belong to R={a/b:p does not divide b}.

grounds.reason: This is the exact definition of R.
F002 ensures the rational coefficients for nonzero generators are nonzero.
S003 explicitly removes powers of p from numerator and denominator.

background_notes.justification: Represent q=A/B with nonzero integers A,B. Successively divide A and B by p while divisible. The positive absolute value strictly decreases at each division, so each process terminates: A=p^α A_0 and B=p^β B_0 for α,β≥0 with p dividing neither A_0 nor B_0. Put d=α−β and u=A_0/B_0. Both u and its inverse have denominators not divisible by p and thus lie in R. The exponent is well defined: two such decompositions with different exponents would, after clearing denominators prime to p, force p to divide a product of integers none divisible by p, contradicting primality.
